content: The man who makes everything that leads to happiness depends upon himself, and not upon other men, has adopted the very best plan for living happily.
author: Plato
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

In Plato's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
